title: Bhatia Was Retired Out. Rodrigues Rescued the First Match. India and England Meet at Taunton With the Series on the Line.
excerpt: The three-match T20I series is tied 1-1. The decider on Tuesday is both teams's final audition before the T20 World Cup begins in England on June 12.
body:
The third and deciding T20I between India and England will be played at Cooper Associates County Ground in Taunton on Tuesday, June 3. The series is locked at 1-1 after two dramatically different matches — the first a statement from India's middle order, the second a reminder that England's spinners remain a force on home soil.

For Indian cricket fans in the United Kingdom, the timing could not be better. The ICC Women's T20 World Cup begins on June 12, with England as hosts. This decider is the last bilateral match for both squads before the tournament, and it doubles as a live audition for the semifinal stage, where India and England are likely to meet again.

## Rodrigues and Bhatia Rescued India From 7 for 2

The first T20I at Chelmsford on May 28 began disastrously for India. Lauren Bell removed both openers in the first over — Smriti Mandhana for a golden duck and Shafali Verma on the last ball — leaving India 7 for 2.

What followed was the partnership of the series. Jemimah Rodrigues, playing with the controlled aggression that has become her signature in T20 cricket, struck 69 off 40 balls. Yastika Bhatia, returning to T20I cricket after a two-year absence, scored 54 off 40 in what was her maiden T20I half-century. Their 126-run stand for the third wicket rebuilt the innings from rubble.

Deepti Sharma added a rapid 22 off 13 as India posted 188 for 7.

Amy Jones hit 67 off 48 for England in the chase, but debutant Nandni Sharma took 3 for 34 — only the second Indian pacer to claim a three-wicket haul on Women's T20I debut — and India won by 38 runs, their second-biggest margin against England in the format.

## Then Bhatia Was Retired Out. A First in Women's Cricket Between Major Nations.

The second T20I at Bristol on May 30 presented a different equation. Freya Kemp smashed an unbeaten 39 off 13 balls to push England to 168 for 5, scoring 24 runs in the final over bowled by Arundhati Reddy. Left-arm spinner Shree Charani was India's best with 3 for 25.

India's chase started well. Mandhana made 32, and the visitors were comfortably placed at 88 for 2 after 11 overs. Then England's three-spinner strategy strangled the middle overs. Charlie Dean, Sophie Ecclestone, and Linsey Smith combined for 3 for 77 from 12 overs, and boundaries dried up completely.

With 60 needed from five overs, Yastika Bhatia — who had crawled to 33 off 36 balls after failing to find the boundary for four consecutive overs — was retired out so Jemimah Rodrigues could come in. It was the first time a batter had been tactically retired out in a women's T20I between two major nations.

The gamble failed. Kemp dismissed Rodrigues on the second ball she faced. India lost six wickets for 33 in the last five overs and fell 26 runs short. "We never thought this situation would come," Harmanpreet Kaur said after the defeat. "Yastika batted really well in the first game. But it is a game — sometimes you click and sometimes you do not."

## What the Decider Means for the World Cup

The T20 World Cup in England begins on June 12. India are expected to face one of England or Australia in the semifinals, and this series has exposed both the promise and the vulnerabilities of Harmanpreet's squad.

The promise: Rodrigues is in sublime form. The batting depth, with Deepti, Reddy, and Ghosh behind the top four, gives India options at every phase. Nandni Sharma's debut performance with the new ball signals a genuine pace option that India have lacked overseas.

The vulnerabilities: the middle-order stall in the second match, the inability to rotate strike against disciplined spin, and the tactical question of where Rodrigues should bat — at number four as she did in the first match, or higher in the order when the situation demands acceleration.

England, for their part, are missing Nat Sciver-Brunt through injury and Danni Wyatt-Hodge on maternity leave. Their power-hitting remains a concern. But Kemp's rise as a death-over finisher, Dean's leadership in the field, and Ecclestone's control in the middle overs make them formidable at home.

## The Taunton Factor

Cooper Associates County Ground has historically been a fair contest between bat and ball. The pitch offers pace and carry early, and the shorter boundaries reward aggressive stroke-making. For India, it is a surface where Mandhana — who averages over 35 in England in T20Is — could be the difference.

For the Indian diaspora in the UK, Tuesday's match is the most accessible live India cricket of the summer before World Cup ticket prices take over. Taunton is a smaller, more intimate ground than the World Cup venues, and Indian fans have a strong recent history of turning up in numbers for women's matches in England.

The series decider is at 6:30 PM BST on Tuesday, June 3. Both teams know the result will carry weight well beyond the bilateral series. The World Cup is eleven days away. This is the last dress rehearsal.
